h1: Driving While License Invalid (DWLI) Lawyer in El Paso
intro: A DWLI ticket means the State says your license was suspended, revoked or expired when you were stopped — and a second one can be a jailable Class B offense. For a flat fee from $59, attorney Robert Navar works on the ticket and the license problem behind it at the same time.
summary: Driving while license invalid is charged under Texas Transportation Code 521.457. A first offense is a Class C misdemeanor (fine only); it can be enhanced to a Class B misdemeanor — up to 180 days in jail — with a prior DWLI conviction or when you drove without insurance and caused a crash with injury.
Most El Paso DWLI tickets trace back to a fixable cause: an OMNI hold from an old unpaid ticket, an unresolved failure-to-appear, a child-support suspension, or a license expired more than two years.
Our strategy is fix the license first, then take proof of a valid license to the prosecutor and ask for a dismissal or deferred disposition so there is no conviction to enhance later.
Flat fees: $59 in El Paso Municipal Court, $69 in Justice of the Peace, Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony courts. Hire online in two minutes.

sections.heading: What a DWLI Charge Means in Texas
paragraphs: "Driving while license invalid" is the Texas name for driving on a suspended, revoked, cancelled or denied license — Transportation Code 521.457. Most people who get this ticket in El Paso did not know their license was invalid. They were pulled over on Gateway East or Zaragoza Road for a tail light, the officer ran the license, and the DPS computer came back "suspended" because of something from a year or two ago.

A first DWLI is a Class C misdemeanor: a fine of up to $500 plus court costs, no jail, filed in municipal or Justice of the Peace court like any other ticket. But the statute has teeth. It becomes a Class B misdemeanor, punishable by up to 180 days in county jail and a fine of up to $2,000, if you have a prior DWLI conviction, or if you were driving without insurance and caused a crash that seriously injured someone. A Class B case is filed in the County Courts at Law at the El Paso County Courthouse, 500 E. San Antonio Ave, and it is a criminal record in the full sense.

That is why the first DWLI matters. If it ends in a conviction, every future stop while your license is still tangled is a potential jail case. If it ends in a dismissal or deferred disposition, there is nothing to enhance. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case.

sections.heading: Why Your License Was Invalid — the Common El Paso Causes
paragraphs: Before we can fight the ticket, we have to know why DPS flagged the license. We pull your driving record the day you hire us, and the answer is almost always one of these.

list.text: an old unpaid ticket was reported under Transportation Code Chapter 706, DPS refused to renew your license until the court clears it, the license expired and you kept driving. See OMNI hold removal.

list.b: Unpaid surcharges from the old Driver Responsibility Program:
list.text: repealed in September 2019, but some drivers never got a new license afterward and still show as expired or suspended.
the Attorney General can suspend a license for unpaid child support; the suspension is lifted by working out a payment arrangement with the AG's office.

list.b: License expired more than two years:
list.text: once a license has been expired long enough that DPS requires you to retest, officers may file DWLI instead of a simple no-license ticket.

list.b: Crash without insurance, DWI, or a points suspension:
list.text: any of these can trigger a DPS suspension you were mailed notice of — at an old address.

sections.heading: Fix the License First: How We Approach a DWLI Ticket
paragraphs: When you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file a notice of appearance the same business day so the DWLI case can't go to warrant while we work. Then we attack the cause. If it's an OMNI hold, we resolve the underlying ticket — often with a warrant recall and a negotiated disposition — and get the court to release the hold. If it's a points or crash suspension, we check whether the period has already run and whether a reinstatement fee is all that stands between you and a valid license. If it's child support, we point you to the right office and form.

Once DPS shows the license as valid, we walk into the pretrial docket with that proof. Prosecutors in El Paso Municipal Court and the JP precincts know the typical DWLI defendant got lost in the system, and they are generally willing to dismiss or offer deferred disposition for a driver who has cleaned up the problem. Where the license can't be restored quickly, we negotiate for deferred disposition anyway so the case ends in dismissal rather than a conviction that could enhance the next one.

For drivers whose suspension still has months to run, an occupational driver's license is often the right move: a court-ordered restricted license under Transportation Code Chapter 521, Subchapter L that lets you drive to work, school and essential errands while the suspension finishes — so your next stop on Loop 375 is not another DWLI.

sections.heading: Class C vs. Class B: Where Your DWLI Case Will Be Heard
paragraphs: A Class C DWLI from El Paso Police is filed in El Paso Municipal Court ($59). One from a DPS trooper, deputy or constable goes to a Justice of the Peace precinct, and Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony tickets go to their municipal courts ($69). In all of them, we can usually resolve the case without you appearing.

If the officer charged the Class B version — because of a prior DWLI or a no-insurance crash — the case is prosecuted by the County Attorney at the County Courthouse. That is a different kind of case with a different fee, and it is exactly what we work to keep you out of by handling the first ticket properly. If you were arrested rather than cited, call us before your first setting; whether the "prior" is really a conviction (and not a dismissed deferral) often decides these cases.

sections.heading: Don't Pay a DWLI Ticket Before You Read This
paragraphs: Paying a DWLI ticket online is a guilty plea, and a DWLI conviction is the one thing that turns your next ticket into a jail case. It also does nothing about the suspension: your license stays invalid, the OMNI hold stays, and the cycle repeats. Instead, check the appearance date on your citation, don't miss it, and send us the ticket through the online hire form. Not sure whether there's already a warrant from an earlier case? The free ticket and warrant lookup will tell you.
Bring whatever you have: the citation, DPS suspension letters, old ticket numbers, child-support correspondence. The more history we can see, the faster we can clear it. Se habla español.

faqs.q: Is driving while license invalid a jailable offense in Texas?
faqs.a: A first DWLI under Transportation Code 521.457 is a Class C misdemeanor — fine only, no jail. It becomes a Class B, with up to 180 days in jail, if you have a prior DWLI conviction or were uninsured and caused a crash with serious injury. Keeping the first one from becoming a conviction is the point of fighting it.

faqs.q: I didn't know my license was suspended. Is that a defense?
faqs.a: It helps, and it's common — DPS mails notices to an address that is often years out of date. More importantly, it tells us where to look: an OMNI hold, an old ticket, or a suspension that may have already expired. We use that history to negotiate a dismissal or deferred disposition.

faqs.q: What is an OMNI hold and how does it cause a DWLI?
faqs.a: OMNI is the Failure to Appear program under Transportation Code Chapter 706. When a court reports an unresolved ticket, DPS refuses to renew your license. If your license then expires and you keep driving, the next stop can be a DWLI. Clearing the ticket releases the hold — see our OMNI hold removal page.

faqs.q: Can I get an occupational license while my DWLI case is pending?
faqs.a: Often, yes. An occupational driver's license is a court-ordered restricted license that lets you drive for work, school and household needs during a suspension. We handle those petitions in El Paso County; see our occupational driver's license page.

faqs.q: Will I have to go to court for a Class C DWLI?
faqs.a: In most cases, no. We appear for you in El Paso Municipal Court, the JP precincts and the area city courts and handle the pretrial negotiation. You would only appear if the case went to trial, which is rare and something we discuss with you first.

faqs.q: What does it cost to hire you for a DWLI ticket?
faqs.a: $59 for El Paso Municipal Court and $69 for JP, Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony courts. Additional citations from the same stop are discounted add-ons, and clearing related warrants is $35 for the first and $20 for each additional.
